I pledge to do my best to stay here, and to help others too. And if it really is beyond me, I pledge to do everything to observe humanity breathe in every moment of the now.
And maybe life is so uncaring for you that your position is so burdened, so difficult, that the last thing you are interested in is the spectacle of humanity changing.

But you and I, it turns out, may not be here to see them. Capital-L Life doesn’t care about you. It is ruthless. It takes the greatest people, and it doesn’t offer an apology. Sometimes, things happen, beyond your control — and one day, you aren’t here anymore.

Seeing one is as close as you get to the process of humanity breathing — inhaling, exhaling. It is surpassed by only few things: maybe the complexity of our universe, and maybe the beauty of a single leaf.
(Obvious caveat for existentially bad paradigm shifts.)
Good news: these shifts tend to be positive. There are catastrophic losers. And we must strive *endlessly* to protect them.
Every human of average lifespan witnesses 1, maybe 2, of these paradigm shifts of humanity.

I will be here to see the rise of China, the rise of the new global middle class, the intelligization of healthcare and materials and education and infrastructure, the decimating effects of climate change, the new geopolitics, the new post-20c status quo.

I will be here to witness humanity adopt entirely new paradigms of how we live, what we do for work, how we love others, what we worry about. And you and I can’t begin to wrap our heads around how that will look in totality.
One of the most infectious, soul-hugging ideas is that I will be alive to see the world fundamentally change — and that I will be wrong about most of it.
